summary.headline: MRVL (-10.25%) and MARA (-10.12%) both RED -- MRVL's post-earnings de-rating deepened to double digits on underwhelming hyperscaler-partnership detail despite raised guidance; MARA's drop vastly outpaced BTC's own modest -0.7% slip, the standing leveraged-beta risk on display. EIX RED and escalating: -4.80% into the final weekend before the Aug-31 wildfire-reform deadline, with the CEO now publicly warning of credit downgrades. A broad but shallow risk-off hit high-multiple/high-beta names (NVDA, ADI, CRDO, FTNT, AEM, HUT, COIN, HOOD, AMBER) following Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, while SPY/QQQ barely moved -- concentrated in exactly the book's higher-beta pockets. LRCX (-5.23%, AMBER) is part of a broader, tier-1-confirmed AI-chip-equipment selloff. SUPV and the prior Dividend-sleeve pullback both resolve to GREEN. CWAN roster-integrity bug hits its 63rd consecutive day -- PRs #11, #12, #14 still unmerged, needs a human decision.

flags.headline: MRVL extends post-earnings slide to -10.25% on the session; now a two-day, thesis-matching de-rating
flags.detail: Marvell beat Q2 FY2027 revenue/EPS estimates and raised its FY2028 revenue target to ~$18B (above its own prior $16.5B threshold), but shares fell further Friday (-10.25% close-to-close, price $216.00 vs $241.29 prior close) on top of Thursday's initial 'sell the news' reaction -- outlook detail on the Google custom-silicon partnership underwhelmed elevated Street hopes. Cumulative decline since the print is now double digits. Tier-1 confirmed: CNBC ("Marvell stock tumbles 6% as outlook underwhelms despite Google deal") and Schaeffer's Investment Research note heavy options activity following the "outlook fumble."
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 53.3x...after a ~150% stock price surge embed extraordinary growth expectations -- any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target or moderation in hyperscaler AI capex would trigger severe multiple compression.' Guidance was not missed (raised above threshold), but the multiple-compression outcome is materializing anyway on underwhelming hyperscaler-partnership detail -- escalated from AMBER (2026-08-28) to RED given the magnitude and persistence.

flags.headline: MARA -10.12% on a session where BTC itself moved only ~-0.7% -- leveraged-beta thesis risk on full display
flags.detail: MARA fell to $10.66 (-10.12%, prev close $11.86) even though bitcoin's own move Friday was modest (BTC slipped below $80,000, down roughly $575/-0.7% on the day per Bloomberg, after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh pledged to fight inflation at Jackson Hole and pushed short-term yields higher). No MARA-specific news found. The equity's ~14x amplification of the underlying BTC move is itself the standing risk, not a new development.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in bitcoin mining means financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of BTC price.' Standing structural risk (GAAP losses, BTC leverage) unchanged -- persisting RED.

flags.headline: EIX down -4.80% as Aug-31 wildfire-reform deadline arrives with no bill passed and CEO warning of credit downgrades
flags.detail: Edison International fell to $70.14 (-4.80%, prev close $73.67) heading into the final weekend before California's Aug-31 legislative session deadline. CEO Pedro Pizarro has publicly warned that California utilities face potential credit downgrades if wildfire liability reform is not passed, and as of this run no draft legislation addressing the state's wildfire costs had been seen. This is now the most time-critical item on the board.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'California's inverse condemnation doctrine holds utilities liable for wildfire damages regardless of negligence, creating a unique and structurally uninsurable business model risk' and the D/E 216% financial-cushion risk. The credit-downgrade warning is the risk materializing in real time, not just a standing structural concern -- persisting from RED (2026-08-28), severity held at RED with escalated urgency given the imminent deadline.

flags.headline: LRCX -5.23% as a broad AI-chip-equipment selloff hits the semicap complex
flags.detail: Lam Research fell to $301.78 (-5.23%, prev close $318.44) as part of a sector-wide selloff -- Micron and SK Hynix fell more than 8%, Sandisk dropped 13%, and semiconductor equipment peers ASML and Applied Materials also declined alongside Lam. No LRCX-specific guidance or news; this is read-across concern about AI-monetization/capex durability, the routine's standing macro watch item.
flags.thesis_link: Matches LRCX key_risk: 'Semiconductor equipment cyclicality...the current AI boom may front-load demand, creating correction risk if AI monetization fails to justify data center capex by 2028.' No guidance cut yet -- held at AMBER, new.

flags.headline: High-multiple growth and crypto-adjacent names sold off broadly on Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks; SPY/QQQ barely moved
flags.detail: NVDA -4.66%, ADI -3.43%, CRDO -3.12%, FTNT -3.91%, AEM -4.24%, HUT -8.83%, COIN -6.43%, HOOD -5.12% -- a broad, catalyst-less-at-the-name-level pullback concentrated in the book's highest-beta / highest-multiple / rate- and crypto-sensitive holdings, while the broad tape was calm (SPY -0.25%, QQQ -0.66%). Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech pledging to bring inflation back to target pushed short-term yields higher and cooled risk-on sentiment. NVDA/FTNT giving back part of Thursday's blowout-earnings rally; AEM tracking gold's modest pullback from its 3-month high (~$4,700 to ~$4,580-4,600) ahead of the same speech; HUT/COIN/HOOD tracking BTC's modest (~-0.7%) slip with outsized equity beta. No individual name's underlying thesis or catalysts changed.
flags.thesis_link: Consistent with each name's own valuation/beta-sensitivity key_risks (high forward P/E multiples for NVDA/ADI/CRDO/FTNT; BTC-price leverage for HUT/COIN/HOOD; gold-price reversion for AEM) but none crossed into thesis-breaking territory today -- AMBER, new, grouped for legibility.

flags.headline: SUPV calm today (-1.07%) after Thursday's -4.22% Argentina-macro-linked decline
flags.detail: No follow-through selling; yesterday's move was the book's largest decliner on no same-day catalyst but matched SUPV's recurring Argentine-macro/credit-quality key_risk despite an improving Q2 (return to profit, NIM expansion). Resolving to GREEN absent further deterioration.

flags.headline: Dividend-sleeve pullback did not persist -- mixed performance today, no broad rotation pattern
flags.detail: Yesterday's catalyst-less 8-name Dividend-sleeve pullback (rotation into AI/growth read) did not continue: SYK +2.66%, VLO +1.69%, ADP +0.99%, ABT +0.77%, GPC +0.50% today, while only ADI (-3.43%) and LRCX (-5.23%) declined meaningfully -- and both of those now trace to the AI-chip-equipment selloff (see LRCX_aichip_selloff), not sector rotation.
